newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin pledges to help troops, improve defence.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin pledges to help troops, improve defence.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin urged the Russian military on Tuesday to support his far-reaching military reform, promising a better life for soldiers and officers and improvements in Russia's defence.
"I believe you will support the reforms being conducted and that you will actively take part in them," the president said in an address to the troops published by his press office.

Yeltsin has said repeatedly that drastic reforms, which include slashing troop numbers, are the only way to relieve the plight of many hungry soldiers and unpaid officers and to improve the nation's defence.

Yeltsin's weekly radio address to the nation last Friday also focused on military problems. Pledges of improvements are the Kremlin's answer to opposition accusations that it is trying to dismember and destroy the much-vaunted Soviet military machine.

"As president and commander-in-chief I assure you -- the reform is aimed at raising Russia's ability to defend itself," Yeltsin said on Tuesday. "Without such a reform Russia's security cannot be provided in the future.

"At the same time the reform will fundamentally improve the social and material well-being of the man in uniform," he went on, reiterating a promise to pay off all wage arrears to the military by September 1.

"In doing so the state will only be repaying what is due. The strategic course is to improve the lot of the military, to restore to the military profession its prestige and the respect of the Russian people."

The 66-year-old president, who is holidaying at Volzhsky Utyos on the Volga river, also repeated plans to merge some units, privatise some defence ministry property and to slash personnel by half a million to 1.2 million by the end of 1998.

Last year, he promised to create a fully professional, non-conscript army by the year 2000, though that deadline appears to have been quietly dropped. The reform, putting the stress on combat readiness and new weapons, will also restructure the strategic command.

Yeltsin wants to turn the armed forces into a smaller and more efficient fighting force after years of declining standards which culminated in humiliation at the hands of separatists in Chechnya last year.
In Tuesday's address, Yeltsin promised to provide officers with 100,000 apartments.

"The task of the armed forces is warfare alone. A military man should not be distracted by having to solve the most simple everyday problems, thinking about how he and his family will manage to survive."
Personnel of military construction units would be cut by 150,000, with civilian construction firms building the bulk of necessary housing, Yeltsin said.
"All issues of life and activity in the armed forces will be at the centre of my attention every day," he said.
